additional_concerns: The four declared missing dependency IDs have no descriptive binding or source hash. Their identities cannot be inferred. The separately supplied JFIU XML schema is missing; missing.jfiu_xml_schema below identifies that dependency without asserting a mapping to those IDs.

The date-only candidate includes filings before 9:00am on 2 February 2026; the launch-based candidates exclude them. The source states both “With effect from 2 February 2026” and a 9:00am launch. Preserve these alternatives pending clarification of “following its implementation” and the governing timezone.
The source directs urgent blackout-period contact; it does not establish that every contact is an STR submission or exempt every actual submission from subsequent duties.

Candidate node.a9c7e7d0e802f5a3fdf2abc2 treats event-associated e-Cert availability as sufficient conditionally. Footnote 3 requires the certificate but does not specify whether availability alone satisfies required use mechanics. Relevant operational authority is missing.
The prescribed PDF and certificate-use instructions are not supplied. A Boolean classification can defer their assessment but cannot establish their contents.
Candidate node.27994712d6e50c0a1c05dea6 has no executable formalization. Its NOT_APPLICABLE correspondence here concerns only the migrated-record access claim.
TRUE_IS_SATISFIED in the resubmission candidates must mean that a trigger exists, not that the resulting duty has been discharged. Later resubmission does not erase the historical trigger.

The conflict-blocking runtime policy is an implementation policy, not a source-imposed restriction. Likewise, OUT_OF_SCOPE for non-submission events differs from a Boolean finding of no trigger; the assessed event domain must remain explicit.
The selected channel, method and e-Cert control does not establish overall XML compliance. The separate schema duty remains supported even where it is outside the assessed question.
